question.prompt: A regular dodecagon (\(12\) sides) is inscribed in a circle with radius \(r\) inches. The area of the dodecagon, in square inches, is:

solutions.explanation:
Join the center \(O\) to all twelve vertices. This partitions the dodecagon into twelve congruent triangles whose interiors do not overlap. Each central angle is \(360^\circ/12=30^\circ\).

Let \(A\) and \(B\) be adjacent vertices. Use the radius \(OA=r\) as the base of triangle \(OAB\), and drop a perpendicular from \(B\) to \(OA\), meeting it at \(H\). The right triangle \(OBH\) has hypotenuse \(OB=r\) and angle \(BOH=30^\circ\), so the side opposite that angle is \(BH=r/2\).

Thus each central triangle has area
\[
\frac12\cdot r\cdot\frac r2=\frac{r^2}{4}.
\]
Adding all twelve areas gives \(12(r^2/4)=\boxed{3r^2}\) square inches, choice A.
solutions.title: Split into twelve triangles
